title: Hillsbrad Foothills
body: For all their green and pastoral beauty, the Hillsbrad Foothills have long been one of the most blood-soaked battlefields in Lordaeron. In the Second War the Horde fell upon the towns here, and afterward the fortress of Durnholde became the heart of the camps where defeated orcs were held, and where a young slave named Thrall was raised before he broke free. When the Third War left the north in ruins, the town of Hillsbrad and the port of Southshore were among the few human communities to survive. Now the Forsaken hold Tarren Mill, where High Executor Darthalia makes war on the humans while the apothecaries test their New Plague on the living. Southshore answers for the Alliance, and dwarves of Dun Garok guard the southeast. Neither side has the land to itself. The Syndicate, outlaws led by the fallen nobles of Alterac, lairs in the ruins of Durnholde, naga and murlocs crowd the beaches, and the ruins of Dalaran and the ogre-held mountains of Alterac lie to the north.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Hillsbrad_Foothills (most blood-soaked battlefield, Second War raids, Forsaken vs Southshore, Syndicate at Durnholde, naga, gnolls, murlocs)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Hillsbrad_Fields (Hillsbrad and Southshore the only parts of Lordaeron not devastated)
quest 500 description (Crushridge ogres in the Ruins of Alterac)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide and nothing from a later era; Thrall's upbringing and escape are backstory a newcomer knows. Earlier: verified

title: Southpoint Tower
body: At the far western end of the foothills, close by the road that climbs toward Silverpine Forest, stands Southpoint Tower, a ruined scout tower overlooking the western fields. Its broken walls still have a use. The Forsaken deathstalker Lesh keeps a lonely watch here, sent to survey the town of Hillsbrad and its fields from a distance. When the moment is right she sends word east to Tarren Mill in a coded phrase, the raven's cry from the west doth beckon, meant for the ears of High Executor Darthalia.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Southpoint_Tower (ruined scout tower at far west end, south of the Silverpine road, Deathstalker Lesh spying on the Alliance)
DB: Deathstalker Lesh 2214 stands in area 285
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Southpoint_Tower (Lesh is female; DB model gender 1)
notes: Converted: what Lesh's coded phrase means (Hillsbrad ripe for attack) moved to part 1 on the turn-in of 494, where Darthalia reads it; the opening keeps the phrase from 494's description. Earlier: Dropped the claim that humans built the tower (no source names the builders).

parts.body: In Tarren Mill the coded phrase is greeted as superb news. To High Executor Darthalia it means that Hillsbrad is ripe for attack, and that the Forsaken can at last carry out their plan of destruction against the town, a step she expects to please Varimathras.

title: Hillsbrad Fields
body: In the west of the foothills lie the orchards and pastures of Hillsbrad, one of the last human farming towns left in Lordaeron. Apple orchards, pumpkins and grazing cattle surround a small town hall, where Magistrate Burnside governs with a town council and his clerk, Horrace Whitesteed. Blacksmith Verringtan and his apprentices arm the townsfolk, and footmen stand guard. Farmer Ray and Farmer Getz own the northern farms, and Ray's dog Stanley keeps him company. The town lives under siege. Raiders from Tarren Mill have marked its farmers, leaders and even its revered proclamation for destruction, and some townsfolk now strike back at the Forsaken from ambush.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Hillsbrad_Fields (apple orchards, pumpkins, cows, Burnside, council, clerk, Verringtan arming militia, ambushes)
quest 502 description (Farmer Ray's little dog Stanley)

DB spawns in area 286: Burnside 2335, Whitesteed 2448, Verringtan 2404, Ray 232, Getz 2403, Stanley 2274, Hillsbrad Footman 2268, Councilman 2387; gameobjects Hillsbrad Proclamation 1761, Town Registry 1759

title: Azurelode Mine
body: Due south of Hillsbrad, the Azurelode Mine cuts into hills that belonged to Gilneas before the Greymane Wall was raised. Today it is worked by the miners of Hillsbrad under Foreman Bonds, with sentries posted to guard them, and its iron feeds the armories of the Alliance. That makes it a prize. The Forsaken war planners in Tarren Mill want it for their own soldiers, and one of its miners, Hackett, is wanted there for the death of a deathstalker.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Azurelode_Mine (part of Gilneas before the Greymane Wall, miners under Foreman Bonds, supplied iron to Alliance armories)
quest 567 description (Miner Hackett wanted for the murder of Deathstalker Fry)

parts.body: Since the draenei joined the Alliance, one of their people in Southshore has taken an interest in the mine's depths. A crate of rare crystals from Azurelode, which the draenei was eager to study, was recently seized on the road by Forsaken raiders, who drove the cart northeast to a tower they are trying to rebuild.
sources: DB: Huraan 17218, faction 1638 (Exodar), in Southshore, starts 9435

title: Darrow Hill
body: Darrow Hill rises in the north of the foothills, beneath the high ground of the Headland on the Alterac border. It is wild country. Vicious gray bears and starving mountain lions prowl its slopes, and yetis come down from the caves above. Somewhere in these hills the wizard Helcular once kept a ritual lair, until a mob from Southshore found and killed him there; the yetis later overran it, and his apprentice believes one of the beasts now carries the dead wizard's rod. Prospectors brave the hill for iron, mithril and truesilver, and for the Alterac granite found in its cave.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Darrow_Hill (northern Hillsbrad right under the Headland, Alterac Granite in the cave on the hill)
quest 552 description (ritual lair in the hills, yeti overtook it, one of the beasts has the rod)

title: Tarren Mill
body: Not long ago Tarren Mill was a thriving human town in the hills of Lordaeron. The Forsaken have since claimed it as their southernmost holding, and it shows the neglect of so many Forsaken places: withered orchards, weathered houses and an old church whose pews now seat the dead. Deathguards patrol the lanes. From here High Executor Darthalia directs the war on Hillsbrad and Southshore, Apothecary Lydon brews toxins for the Dark Lady's New Plague, and captured farmers are kept in a room close by. Other peoples of the Horde pass through as well, among them the orc Krusk, here on the Warchief's business.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Tarren_Mill (once a thriving human town, Forsaken seized it, church, withered orchards, poor repair)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Hillsbrad_Foothills (Sunwell Trilogy: still human after the Third War, then the Forsaken's southernmost holding)
quest 9425 description and reward text (blood elves supporting the Forsaken)

parts.body: Since the blood elves joined the Horde, Silvermoon has sent envoys to Tarren Mill as well. Advisor Duskingdawn greets each newcomer from Quel'Thalas and urges them to do all they can for their new Forsaken allies, so that the Forsaken will be the more willing to help the sin'dorei in turn.
sources: npc_text 8789 (gossip menu 7358, Duskingdawn: do as much as possible for these people)

title: Southshore
body: Southshore began as a small fishing village and grew into a busy military port in the Second War, when the Horde captured it and the Alliance later rebuilt it. It remains one of the last pockets of human civilization in Lordaeron. Magistrate Henry Maleb governs the town, his predecessor killed by assassins, while Marshal Redpath leads the guard against the Forsaken of Tarren Mill, the Syndicate and the ogres of Alterac. Life goes on regardless. Folk travel from as far as Darkshire for Chef Jessen's turtle bisque, Merideth Carlson breeds horses, Loremaster Dibbs pores over books saved from Alterac, and the dwarven Brewmeister Bilger takes old debts in moonshine. In the cemetery lies Helcular, a wizard the townsfolk killed.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Southshore (fishing village, Second War military port captured by the Horde and rebuilt, one of the few pockets of human civilization)
quest greeting 2263 (Redpath: the Horde, the Syndicate and the Ogres)
quest 552 description (Helcular buried in Southshore cemetery)

Earlier: Replaced the unsupported claim that the brewmeister supplies the inn with what quest 647 shows (a debt repaid in moonshine).

title: Western Strand
body: West of Southshore, the Western Strand runs along the shore where the foothills meet the sea. It belongs to the Torn Fin murlocs, whose coastrunners, muckdwellers, tidehunters and oracles crowd its beaches and shallows, and a murloc called Scargil is sometimes seen among them. Marshal Redpath wants the creatures thinned before they trouble the town, though the officer he gave the task to regards hunting overgrown fish as beneath him. The Forsaken of Tarren Mill find a use for the murlocs too, for their apothecaries prize Torn Fin eyes in their brews. Wreckage drifts in the water offshore.
sources: DB spawns in area 295: Torn Fin Coastrunner, Muckdweller, Oracle, Tidehunter; Scargil 14276 rank 4; Schooner Wreckage pools
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Earlier: verified

title: Purgation Isle
body: Off the southwestern coast of the foothills lies Purgation Isle, an island that belonged to the kingdom of Kul Tiras before the First War. Nothing living holds it now. Its shores are haunted by condemned human and dwarf spirits that cannot find peace in death: paladins and justicars under a curse, clerics, monks and acolytes, and mages who writhe in torment. Who they were in life, and what crime or curse bound them to the island, is not recorded. The ogre necromancer Kormok is said to have delighted in calling these restless dead to do his bidding.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Purgation_Isle (Kul Tiras before the First War, condemned human and dwarf spirits unable to find peace, recent history unknown, Kormok)
DB spawns in area 896: Cursed Paladin 7071, Cursed Justicar 7072, Condemned Cleric 7070, Monk 7069, Acolyte 7068, Writhing Mage 7075
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Earlier: Location reworded to match the wiki (south of the shore, southwestern Hillsbrad). Kormok line kept as hearsay, matching the wiki's own 'is said to'.

title: Nethander Stead
body: East of Southshore, south of Tarren Mill on the far side of the river, lies Nethander Stead, a farm that has passed out of human hands. Its fields now belong to the Mudsnout gnolls, a tribe found nowhere else, whose shamans move among the overgrown furrows, and a gnoll called Ro'Bark is sometimes seen among them. Something else has taken root in the abandoned fields: Mudsnout Blossoms, giant pale mushrooms with a horrible reek. Apothecary Lydon of Tarren Mill prizes them as the base of one of his deadliest elixirs, and considers them the one good thing the gnolls have ever done.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Nethander_Stead (farm east of Southshore, only location of the Mudsnout tribe, giant white mushrooms in the abandoned fields)
quest 509 description and reward text (south of Tarren Mill, east of the river and Southshore; horrible reek; those filthy gnolls are good for something)
DB spawns in area 289: Mudsnout Gnoll 2372, Mudsnout Shaman 2373, Ro'Bark 14278 rank 4, Mudsnout Blossom 1723
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Earlier: Removed the unsupported claim that its people are long gone; the wiki only says the fields are abandoned and overrun.

title: Durnholde Keep
body: Southeast of Tarren Mill, across the river, stand the ruins of Durnholde Keep. After the Second War the fortress served as the command center of the internment camps where defeated orcs were held, under the self-absorbed drunkard Lieutenant General Aedelas Blackmoore. Here Blackmoore raised an orphaned orc infant as a slave and pit fighter and named him Thrall, and here Taretha Foxton helped him escape. Thrall later returned, slew Blackmoore and called on the spirit of the earth to bring the keep down. Its ruins now shelter the Syndicate: watchmen, rogues and shadow mages who gather the blood of innocents, while their jailors keep captured orcs in chains.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Durnholde_Keep (internment camp command center, Blackmoore, Thrall's upbringing and escape with Taretha's help, Thrall leveled it, Syndicate outpost)
quest 498 description (southeast of Tarren Mill across the river)
DB spawns in area 275: Syndicate Watchman, Shadow Mage, Rogue; Drull 2239 and Tog'thar 2238 with Locked ball and chain; Jailor Eston 2427 and Jailor Marlgen 2428
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Durnholde_Keep (Spirit of the Earth leveled the fortress)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: Thrall's upbringing, escape with Taretha's help and the keep's fall are backstory a newcomer knows from the Second War's aftermath, not something a quest here reveals; the orcs in chains are the situation of quest 498. Old Hillsbrad (Caverns of Time) is not mentioned. Earlier: verified

title: Eastern Strand
body: Southeast of Southshore, the Eastern Strand belongs to the naga. Daggerspine shorehunters, shorestalkers, sirens and screamers have come up out of the sea to claim its beaches and shallows, and a naga called Lady Zephris is sometimes seen among them. Their arrival troubles more than the local garrison. Word has reached the Alliance High Command that the naga are a growing threat, and Marshal Redpath has ordered his lieutenant to deal with them. The Forsaken see opportunity instead: the apothecaries of Tarren Mill want daggerspine scales for their poisons.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Eastern_Strand (southeast coast, home of the Daggerspine naga on the beaches and in the water)
quest 562 description (Alliance High Command concerned about the naga)
DB spawns in area 294: Daggerspine Shorehunter, Shorestalker, Siren, Screamer; Lady Zephris 14277 rank 4
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Earlier: verified

title: Dun Garok
body: In the southeastern hills, set against Thoradin's Wall, stands Dun Garok, a dwarven keep whose garrison helps protect the humans of Hillsbrad and the Azurelode Mine. Captain Ironhill commands its mountaineers, riflemen and priests, and its barracks keep kegs of Shindigger Stout on hand. The Forsaken loathe the dwarves' presence, and the dwarves give as good as they get: their scouts once raided a Deathguard's camp and walked off with his sword. A Stormpike named Tamra is sometimes found within its walls.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Dun_Garok (dwarven keep in the southeastern hills, helped protect the humans and the Azurelode Mine, Forsaken loathed the dwarves)
quest 541 description (barracks along Thoradin's Wall, Captain Ironhill)
DB spawns in area 290: Captain Ironhill 2304, Dun Garok Mountaineer, Rifleman, Priest, Tamra Stormpike 14275 rank 2, Keg of Shindigger Stout 1727
notes: Check: Darthalia making the keep her last target names how the Horde chain ends (26722 holds it to part 4), so it moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 539, where 541 is offered; Horde-only part on a faction 0 entry). Converted: the siege itself is told in 26722 part 5. Earlier: verified

parts.body: To High Executor Darthalia, the dwarves who aid the humans are the last obstacle in the foothills. Once Hillsbrad's town and its mine have been struck, she names the barracks at Dun Garok, and Captain Ironhill with them, as the final mission of her Battle of Hillsbrad.
sources: quest 541 description (offered at the turn-in of 539)

title: Thoradin's Wall
body: Along the eastern edge of the foothills runs Thoradin's Wall, raised long ago by King Thoradin of Arathor near his capital of Strom to shield humanity from the Amani trolls. It still divides Hillsbrad from the Arathi Highlands, though the centuries have left it heavily damaged and in ruins, its great stones broken in many places. Gray bears and moss creepers wander beneath its shadow, and the dwarves of Dun Garok have built their barracks against it, so that the ancient barrier still shelters a garrison of the Alliance.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Thoradin's_Wall (built by Thoradin near Strom against the Amani, separates Arathi from Hillsbrad, heavily damaged and in ruins in original WoW, has a gateway)
quest 541 description (Dun Garok along Thoradin's Wall)
DB spawns in area 1057: Elder Gray Bear, Giant Moss Creeper
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Earlier: Removed the gateway (the wiki's gate is in the Old Hillsbrad instance) and the interpretive 'last line' claim.

title: High Executor Darthalia
body: High Executor Darthalia commands Tarren Mill, and she reminds all who stand before her that she answers to the dreadlord Varimathras and the Dark Lady. Her charge, as she gives it, is to quell what she calls the human infestation until the apothecaries finish their New Plague, and her orders show no mercy: farms to be raided, peasants hunted through the orchards, Hillsbrad's blacksmith and magistrate marked for death, and Southshore to be razed once Hillsbrad falls. She pays the bounties on Hillsbrad's most dangerous townsfolk, on the Syndicate's thugs and on the Syndicate noble Baron Vardus. She has no patience for idleness or chatter, and soldiers who loiter in Tarren Mill are told she can behead them for treason.
sources: npc_text 16667 (You will speak when spoken to)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/High_Executor_Darthalia (under Varimathras and Sylvanas, stop the spread of humans in Hillsbrad)
notes: Converted: nothing moved: her targets are orders, and their fall is told in 26722. Her command under Varimathras is now her own claim (quests 527, quest greeting 2215), so it stays true after the Battle for the Undercity; the campaign is framed as orders rather than deeds done. Earlier: Bounty line reworded: the Syndicate bounty is posted by Sylvanas's authority and paid by Darthalia (quest 549).

title: Apothecary Lydon
body: Apothecary Lydon of the Royal Apothecary Society is, in the judgment of Master Apothecary Faranell, one of the Society's most dedicated and skilled members. He is also profoundly gloomy. Fresh air and blooming flowers sour his mood, and only suffering brightens his day. He tests his elixirs on Umpi, the frog he calls his assistant, poisoning and reanimating her over and over, and he longs for the day the Dark Lady's New Plague brings the world the death he thinks it deserves. His skill is known well beyond Lordaeron: Apothecary Zamah of Thunder Bluff counts him a colleague worth sending for.
sources: quest 501 description (the New Plague brings this world the death it deserves)
notes: Check: part 3 trimmed to a brief mention, since thunder_bluff.json (Forsaken Aid, 163815) tells the toxin, its blood of innocents and its use in Stonetalon in full; QUEST_DONE 1066 kept as its trigger (Thunder Bluff's entry uses only 1064). Converted: the poisoned treat for Stanley moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 502, where Stanley is fed), the tainted keg for the farmers to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 524), and the Stonetalon toxin to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 1066, its brewing; the Forsaken Aid chain is told in thunder_bluff.json, which uses only 1064, so 1065 and 1066 stay here). Opening keeps Faranell's praise, his gloom, Umpi and his link to Zamah (quest 1065). Earlier: verified

parts.body: His Elixir of Pain, brewed from mountain lion blood, is tried on Farmer Ray's little dog Stanley in Hillsbrad Fields. The dog sniffs the treat, eagerly digs in, and swells into an enraged beast that turns on anyone near it.
sources: smart_scripts 2274 (Stanley becomes Enraged Stanley and attacks)

parts.body: His Elixir of Agony, highly contagious, is too fine a plague to waste on a frog or a dog. Poured into a keg of Shindigger Stout stolen from the dwarves of Dun Garok, it is left on the rug for the captured farmers of Tarren Mill, whom Darthalia gave over to his disposal.

Even distant Stonetalon has need of his craft. When a note from Zamah reaches Tarren Mill telling of the Horde's need against the Venture Company there, Lydon knows exactly what to do, and he soon has a toxin ready for her, brewed from one of the darkest ingredients the foothills can offer.

title: Krusk
body: Krusk is one of a party of orc warriors sent by Warchief Thrall to investigate the Syndicate in Hillsbrad and to recover an object from Durnholde Keep. The Syndicate surprised them in the ruins and overwhelmed them by sheer numbers. Krusk fought his way free, but some of his comrades were taken captive, Drull and Tog'thar among them, and are held at Durnholde still. Now Krusk waits among the Forsaken of Tarren Mill, gathering any word of the captives and of the trinket the Warchief wants. The place weighs on him, for the Warchief was born and raised close by.
sources: quest greeting 2229 (the place the Warchief was born and raised lies so close)
notes: Converted: Gol'dir carried off elsewhere moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 498, where Krusk learns it); Perenolde's plans and the pendant to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 506); the pendant's return to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 508). QUEST_DONE 503 and QUEST_ACCEPT 507 are left to alterac.json (Gol'dir, Perenolde). Opening says only that some comrades were taken, as quest 498's description does. Earlier: Softened the birthplace line to follow Krusk's greeting rather than naming Durnholde as Thrall's birthplace.

parts.body: Drull and Tog'thar are freed from their chains, and Krusk swears to show the humans what comes of trying to make slaves of orc warriors. Their leader Gol'dir is not among them: the Syndicate has taken him somewhere else, and for now Krusk has no clue where.

Gol'dir's word reaches him at last. The Syndicate's leader, Aliden Perenolde, means to enslave the orcs who stand against him, and his mistress wears the very pendant the Warchief desires. Krusk is outraged and takes up both causes as one: Perenolde must die, and the trinket will be theirs.

With the pendant in his hands, Krusk admits it is strange that the Warchief would spend so much over so small a thing. He does not claim to understand Thrall, but he will follow him whatever his commands, and he is sure the Warchief will be glad of the news.

title: Magistrate Henry Maleb
body: Henry Maleb came to Southshore as its new magistrate after his predecessor was assassinated. He was elated to win such a commission so early in his career, though he now wonders if he would have been better off shuffling papers in Stormwind. His suspicion fell at once on the Syndicate, the thieves led by the fallen nobles of Alterac, and he sends fighters against their camps in the hills. The town crier's warnings of assassins in the hills keep his guards on edge. He meets attackers defiantly, crying that they will never take back Alterac, or Southshore.
sources: creature_text 2435 (Southshore Crier: they must be after the Magistrate again)
notes: Converted: the seized plans moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 510) and the contract naming Maleb to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 522). Opening keeps his arrival, his suspicion and his defiance; the crier's alarms added from creature_text 2435. Earlier: verified. No TALK trigger on purpose: faction template 96 has no enemy group, so Horde could open his dialog; all triggers are Alliance-only quests.

parts.body: Papers taken from the Syndicate camps prove his suspicion right. The brigands were gathering masks, oil and poison for an important mission against Southshore, and Maleb concludes that the band of cutthroats has made war on his town.

Then a sealed contract makes it personal. The Syndicate wants Maleb himself dead, just as he believes it wanted the magistrate before him, and the latest attack on Southshore was aimed at him. He resolves to strike at the Syndicate's noble leaders before their plans are realized.

title: Marshal Redpath
body: Marshal Redpath commands the defense of Southshore, and he has his hands full. The Horde holds Tarren Mill, the Syndicate prowls the hills, and the Crushridge ogres who seized the ruins of Alterac may yet push down into the foothills and arrive at Southshore's front door. Redpath means to keep them at bay, posting bounties on ogres and sending fighters into the ruins to bloody the noses of the warmongers. Closer to home he wants the murlocs of the Western Strand culled and the naga of the Eastern Strand put down, though the officer he trusts with that work is far less eager than he is.
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide; Farren's reluctance is shown in quest 536's own description. Earlier: verified

title: Lieutenant Farren Orinelle
body: Lieutenant Farren Orinelle was transferred to Southshore from the Stormwind city guard, and he has not forgiven anyone for it. He passes his days at the inn calling for more ale, complaining about the smell of the harbor and mocking Marshal Redpath's orders to clear out the murlocs of the Western Strand, which he gladly leaves to others. He cannot bear to touch the slimy creatures, and he has not eaten fish in weeks, which in Southshore means hardly eating at all. All he truly wants is to see Stormwind again.
sources: quests 536, 559, 561, 562, 563 descriptions, request and reward texts
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Southshore (Farren at the inn mocking Redpath)
DB: Farren 2228 faction template 12, spawned in the Southshore inn
notes: Converted: his scheme for a transfer moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 561, where he explains it and offers 562); Samuelson's answer to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 563, at Samuelson 2439 in Stormwind; not used by the Stormwind file). Opening keeps his transfer, the inn, the murlocs and his distaste for fish (quest 559 reward text). Earlier: verified

parts.body: When Redpath turns him toward the naga of the Eastern Strand, Farren sees his chance. His old mentor has written that Alliance High Command is worried about the naga, and that whoever proves useful against them may win promotion, or at least reassignment. Farren admits the naga are too much for him, and asks others to win his victories for him.

His report, carried quietly so Redpath will not catch on, reaches Major Samuelson, the new captain of the Stormwind guard and once Farren's mentor. Samuelson is pleased to see his attentive pupil apply himself to the naga, and promises to weigh it when he next reviews personnel assignments.

title: Phin Odelic
body: Phin Odelic leads a small band of adventurers who look into the strange happenings around Hillsbrad. His suspicions took hold when his cousin in Hillsbrad had to put down his dog Stanley, after the animal swelled to an unnatural size and savagely attacked anyone who came near. Phin is sure the undead are behind it, and he sent two of his companions, Quae and Kinelory, to spy on the Go'Shek Farm in the Arathi Highlands. They speak of him with deep affection, for since the plague he has given them the friends and family they never thought they would find again.
sources: quest 657 reward text (Quae: since the plague, friends or family)
DB: Phin 2711 faction template 12, in Southshore
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide: his cousin's dog and his companions' errand are quest 659's premise; what they find is told in 26724. Earlier: verified. Cousin left unnamed; Stanley is Farmer Ray's dog, but no source calls Ray his cousin.

title: Loremaster Dibbs
body: Loremaster Dibbs keeps his books in Southshore, the town that lies closest to the ruins of Alterac. He mourns the knowledge lost when that kingdom fell and the ogres moved into its halls, and he works with Milton Sheaf of the Royal Library in Stormwind to recover the tomes that survive, keeping back one ancient book of troll lore, the Arm of Gri'lek, for his own study. Every scrap of strange writing that trickles down from the mountains lands on his desk. Ciphers beyond his skill go on to Prospector Stormpike in Ironforge. His old bones, he admits, would never survive the climb himself.
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Earlier: Removed 'scholar of the old kingdoms' (unsupported); quest 538 says Southshore is the closest town to the ruins, not that Dibbs is the closest person.

title: The Battle of Hillsbrad
body: High Executor Darthalia of Tarren Mill says she acts under the direct command of Varimathras: the Forsaken are to quell the humans of the foothills until the apothecaries can develop the New Plague. Deathstalker Lesh watches the town of Hillsbrad from Southpoint Tower, and Darthalia's information marks it as vulnerable. She means to break it in stages, beginning with its food and its infrastructure. Raiders are sent west against the northernmost farms of Hillsbrad Fields, with orders that the landowners, Farmer Ray and Farmer Getz, be executed as well. Every soldier is reminded that dawdling in Tarren Mill while there is work to be done elsewhere will not be forgiven.
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of 494 and 527. Parts follow the chain: 1 farms fallen and peasants hunted (QUEST_DONE 527), 2 the smith (QUEST_DONE 529), 3 Burnside, council and registry (QUEST_DONE 532), 4 Azurelode (QUEST_DONE 539), 5 Dun Garok and the commendation (QUEST_DONE 541). Varimathras's command is Darthalia's word, so it stays true after the Battle for the Undercity. 14351 (ends at Bragor Bloodfist in the Undercity) not used as a trigger; 550 is disabled. Earlier: verified

parts.body: The northern farms are raided and their owners slain, and word of the attack sends the townsfolk into a panic. Deathstalkers report peasants fleeing to the orchards of southern Hillsbrad in hope of escaping their doom, and Darthalia sends her soldiers after them to lay them waste in the Dark Lady's name.

The grip of death tightens, yet the humans resist harder than expected, armed by Blacksmith Verringtan. So the smith is executed and his apprentices with him, and a shipment of iron is carried off from his stockpile, kept for the day Hillsbrad is conquered and the razing of Southshore begins.

Despite their losses, the townsfolk rally around their leaders. Magistrate Burnside and the town council are slain, the revered Hillsbrad Proclamation is destroyed and the town registry stolen. The registry gives away one more target: the Azurelode Mine, a prime source of iron for the Alliance armories, which the Alliance still guards fervently.

Foreman Bonds and his miners are slain, and Darthalia expects the Dark Lady to be pleased with a new mine from which to arm her soldiers. One obstacle remains. Dwarves have come to the aid of the humans, and their barracks at Dun Garok, along Thoradin's Wall, become the final mission of the battle.

Dun Garok is besieged and Captain Ironhill falls with his mountaineers, riflemen and priests. Darthalia counts the deed worthy of the highest praise, and those who see the campaign through carry her sealed commendation to the Undercity, so that the high command may recognize their heroics.

title: The Apothecary's Elixirs
body: In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon serves the Dark Lady's hunger for a New Plague, one meant for humans and Scourge alike, through a series of ever crueler elixirs. Each begins with a killing agent gathered from the foothills. Gray bear tongues and rare creeper ichor are wanted for one brew, the blood of mountain lions for another, and for a third the Mudsnout Blossoms that grow in the abandoned fields of Nethander Stead, south of the town. Lydon, who finds every bright day in Hillsbrad a misery, means to test each one, and his long-suffering frog Umpi is always first in line.
sources: smart_scripts 2274 (Stanley becomes Enraged Stanley and attacks)
quest 659 description (dog grew to immense size and attacked)
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of the three entry quests (496, 501, 509). Parts: 1 the Elixir of Suffering and Umpi (QUEST_DONE 496), 2 Stanley (QUEST_DONE 502), 3 the composite and Faranell (QUEST_DONE 513, at Faranell in the Undercity; the Undercity file uses only TALK 2055), 4 the tainted keg (QUEST_DONE 524). Earlier: Reworded the opening so it does not echo Silverpine's 'A Recipe for Death'. Facts verified against quests 496 to 524.

parts.body: The tongues and ichor become what Lydon calls an Elixir of Suffering, and Umpi gets the first taste of what the Dark Lady has planned. Nothing, he says, brightens a gloomy day in these miserable foothills like bringing a little suffering into the world.
sources: quest 499 description (offered on the turn-in of 496)

parts.body: Mountain lion blood becomes the Elixir of Pain, which Lydon hopes could be the start of something very beautiful for Lady Sylvanas. Its test is Farmer Ray's little dog Stanley in Hillsbrad Fields, who eagerly digs in and swells into a raging beast.
sources: smart_scripts 2274 (Stanley becomes Enraged Stanley and attacks)

parts.body: The Elixir of Agony takes longer. Lydon mixes the blossoms into a composite and sends it to the Undercity, where Master Apothecary Faranell, delighted with his colleague's thinking, applies his colloid of decay. To activate it Lydon needs a strong troll's blood potion, daggerspine scales from the naga and torn fin eyes from the murlocs of the southern coast.

The finished plague, highly contagious, is too good to waste on a frog or a dog. It is poured into a keg of Shindigger Stout stolen from the dwarves of Dun Garok, and the tainted keg is left on the rug in the room where the Deathguards hold their captured farmers.

title: Hints of a New Plague
body: Word of strange events in Hillsbrad has reached Phin Odelic in Southshore, who leads a small band of adventurers looking into them. His cousin in Hillsbrad had to put down his dog, after the animal grew to monstrous size and turned savage on anyone who came near, and Phin suspects the undead. Looking for proof, he sent two of his companions, Quae and Kinelory, to watch the Go'Shek Farm in the Arathi Highlands, where the Horde is at work. They have not checked in for days, and Phin, who worries for them, wants them found.
notes: Converted: the opening is quest 659's premise. Parts: 1 the pair found and the courier (QUEST_DONE 659), 2 Jorell's experiments (QUEST_DONE 658), 3 the stolen research (QUEST_DONE 660), 4 Phin's relief and resolve (QUEST_DONE 661). The Go'Shek quests are not used by arathi.json, whose Go'Shek Farm entry only mentions the watchers. Earlier: Softened the ending: quest 661 says the research only gives Phin an idea of what is going on.

parts.body: Quae and Kinelory are found keeping quiet watch, for orcs do not take kindly to spies, and there is more to Go'Shek than meets the eye. Kinelory has seen a courier slip out of a small house to the south, and the pair believe the courier carries notes to Tarren Mill.

The courier's sealed folder is taken and opened. It shows that a Forsaken, Apothecary Jorell, has been working on deadly experiments at Go'Shek. Quae cannot yet say what that has to do with Hillsbrad, but Phin would not want it to continue, and Kinelory means to steal whatever research Jorell has not yet sent to Tarren Mill.

Under guard, Kinelory creeps down to the farm and comes back with what she could carry off, little the worse for it. The items should at least give Phin an idea of what is going on in Arathi, and the pair stay on a while to watch for retaliation.

In Southshore, Phin laughs with relief to hear that his two troublemakers are alive, for they are irreplaceable as friends and traveling companions. With their findings in hand, he hopes his band will soon learn what the Forsaken are up to, and put an end to it.

title: Taretha's Gift
body: Warchief Thrall has sent a band of orc warriors to the Hillsbrad Foothills with two tasks: to investigate the human brigands called the Syndicate, and to recover something from Durnholde Keep, the fortress where he was raised a slave. The mission has gone badly. The Syndicate surprised the orcs in the ruins and overwhelmed them by sheer numbers. Krusk fought his way free to Tarren Mill, but others were taken captive, their leader Gol'dir among them, and Drull and Tog'thar lie in chains at Durnholde. Krusk gathers what word he can of the captives and of the small trinket the Warchief wants.
sources: item 3498 Taretha's Necklace (a crescent moon on a silver chain)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Taretha's_Necklace (Taretha gave it to Thrall; later held by Elysa, delivered to Krusk)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Taretha's_Necklace (Taretha gave Thrall the necklace when he escaped Durnholde)
notes: Check: Taretha moved from the opening into part 4 (QUEST_DONE 507), since with the title her name beside the Warchief's trinket tied the pendant to her early; Gol'dir named in the opening as a captive (quest 533 description) so parts 2 and 3 read on even without part 1. Converted: the opening is the setup of 498 and 533, with Taretha kept only as the backstory of Thrall's escape. Parts: 1 the two freed and Gol'dir missing (QUEST_DONE 498), 2 Gol'dir's whereabouts (QUEST_DONE 533), 3 his news of Perenolde and Elysa (QUEST_ACCEPT 506, at Gol'dir once freed), 4 Perenolde's death and the pendant as Taretha's necklace (QUEST_DONE 507, at Elysa), 5 Krusk's reaction (QUEST_DONE 508). QUEST_DONE 503, QUEST_ACCEPT 507 and the kills of Perenolde and Gol'dir's talk are left to alterac.json. Earlier: verified

parts.body: Drull and Tog'thar are freed, split up by their captors but unbroken, and each makes his own way back to Tarren Mill. The humans meant to make slaves of them. Their leader Gol'dir is not with them: the Syndicate has carried him off to some other place, and for now no one knows where.

Word and rumor at last point to the large Syndicate camp north of Tarren Mill, and papers taken there settle it. Gol'dir has been moved from place to place, but now he is held in a large Syndicate base further north, most likely in the Alterac Mountains.

Gol'dir is found in chains, kept at hauling and digging, and he counts his suffering as nothing beside the news he carries. The Syndicate's leader, Lord Aliden Perenolde, came to boast of enslaving the orcs who stand against him, as his father and his mentor Blackmoore once planned. Around the neck of his mistress, a wisp of a girl named Elysa, hung the pendant the Warchief desires.

Perenolde is slain at his manor on the shores of Lordamere Lake. Elysa, terrified, begs for her life, swearing he kept her against her will, and gladly gives up the pendant, wanting no memory of him. It is a crescent moon on a silver chain: the necklace once given to Thrall by Taretha Foxton, the human girl who helped him escape Durnholde.
sources: quest 507 description, objectives and reward text

parts.body: Krusk takes the necklace and finds it strange that the Warchief would spend so much over so small a thing. He does not claim to understand Thrall, but he will follow him whatever his commands, and the Warchief will surely be glad to hear the pendant is safe.

title: Helcular's Revenge
body: Helcular was a wizard of the foothills who sought to become a lich. He was close to completing the change when a lynch mob from Southshore found his ritual lair in the hills, killed him, and buried him in their own cemetery. His apprentice, Novice Thaivand, now dwells among the Forsaken of Tarren Mill and has sworn that the rains of vengeance will fall on Southshore. First the wizard's rod must be taken back, for yetis overran the ritual lair after his death, and Thaivand is sure one of the beasts carries it.
sources: creature_text 2433 (Helcular's Remains: Southshore shall pay in blood)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Helcular (mage, lich ritual, lynch mob from Southshore, Thaivand)
DB: Flames of Azel 1768 and Veraz 1769 in area 1680, Uzel 1770 in area 1683
notes: Converted: the pyres and the plan for the grave moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 552, where Thaivand offers 553); the rising of Helcular's remains to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 553, at Helcular's Grave 1767). Earlier: verified

parts.body: With the rod recovered, Thaivand reveals the rest. Helcular fashioned three ceremonial pyres for his most powerful spell: the Flames of Azel and Veraz in the Foothill Caverns, and the Flame of Uzel in a cave higher in the mountains. Charged from all three, the rod is to be driven into Helcular's grave in heavily guarded Southshore.

The charged rod is driven into the grave, which teems with mystical energy, and a great rumbling rises from the ground. Helcular's remains climb out of the earth, crying that they have risen from the grave and that Southshore shall pay in blood for the death it dealt him.

title: Southshore and the Syndicate
body: Southshore's last magistrate was assassinated, and though the killers were never found, his successor Henry Maleb is all but certain the Syndicate hired them: a gang of thieves led by villainous nobles of fallen Alterac. The Syndicate keeps camps at Sofera's Naze and Corrahn's Dagger, north and west of Tarren Mill, and Maleb wants the thugs there cut down. The camps hold more than cutthroats. Lists, letters and orders pass through them, and whatever is taken from the Syndicate may tell Southshore what the brigands intend. Maleb fears they are not finished with his town.
sources: creature_text 2435 (Southshore Crier: assassins after the Magistrate again)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Syndicate (Alterac nobles, Argus Wake secretly controlled the Syndicate)
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of 505 and of the documents found in the camps. Parts: 1 the plans and Maleb's war (QUEST_DONE 510), 2 the contract and Vardus (QUEST_DONE 522; 523 offered at once), 3 the decrypted letter and Nagaz (QUEST_DONE 525), 4 Vardus's death (QUEST_DONE 523), 5 Nagaz's death and his hidden master (QUEST_DONE 537). The two deaths are split because either can come first. QUEST_ACCEPT 523 and 537 and the kills of Vardus and Nagaz are left to alterac.json. Earlier: Added the chain's resolution (quests 523, 537). Owned by Hillsbrad; Alterac drops its copies. Fix: part 1 adds the list's signature, Baron V., Quartermaster, as page_text 371 gives it (item 3718, carried during quest 510, read by Maleb on the turn-in); the initial is not expanded, so Vardus stays unnamed until part 2 (QUEST_DONE 522) and alterac.json 3616 keeps its contract reveal.

parts.body: One seized list, signed only Baron V., Quartermaster, calls for food, weapons and clothing, and for masks, oil and poison, urgently needed for an important mission against Southshore. Maleb concludes that the brigands have made war on his town, and orders strikes on the ruins of Strahnbrad, where Alterac's nobles hide among common agents, betrayed only by the signet rings they wear.
sources: page_text 371 (Foreboding Plans, item 3718, the StartItem of quest 510: signed Baron V., Quartermaster)

parts.body: A contract sealed in red wax with a distinctive signet explains the latest attack: it orders the death of Maleb himself, and he is sure the Syndicate struck at the magistrate before him the same way. It bears the name of Baron Vardus, a noble of Alterac known for a cold heart and brutal practices, and Maleb wants him found and brought to justice.

Stranger still is an encrypted letter that Loremaster Dibbs cannot read and passes to Prospector Stormpike in Ironforge. Decoded, it proves to be no thief's or noble's work. It was written by Nagaz of the Argus Wake, a power that seems to stand behind the Syndicate itself, and Maleb sends fighters into the Uplands to find him and his shadow mages.

Baron Vardus is hunted down among the Syndicate haunts of Alterac, and his head is laid before Maleb in Southshore. The magistrate admits he rests a little easier knowing that the villain who ordered his death has lost his own head.

Nagaz and his shadow mages fall in the Uplands. Maleb takes little comfort from it, for Nagaz was merely the servant of another. The Argus Wake, he fears, may run deep through the continent of Azeroth, or even the world, and no one in Southshore can say how far.
